references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, it describes how the plague of frogs came upon Egypt as God had warned through Moses.
Moses prayed to the Lord to remove the frogs after Pharaoh's request, and verse 9 shows the fulfillment of this prayer.
It shows a similar pattern where the Lord does as Moses asks by removing the swarms of flies from Egypt.
A parallel case where Moses prays to the Lord, and the plague (hail) stops in response to his prayer.
The Lord does as Moses asks and removes the locusts from Egypt, just as the frogs were removed.
Moses prays to the Lord, and the fire stops - showing the same pattern of intercession and God's answer.
The psalm recalls the plague of frogs in Egypt as part of God's mighty deeds.
It creates a theological contrast between God's immediate action in judging Egypt and the people who must obey to inherit the land.
It confirms the same theological principle that God's actions follow His word exactly, highlighting the role of the prophets.
It creates a theological contrast between the animal that brings judgment (the frogs) and the animal that brings salvation (the fish).
